facts.text: I have lumps in my neck.
They're on the right side of my neck, toward the front.
I've been on maintenance hemodialysis for 3 years.
My kidneys failed because of chronic glomerulonephritis.

aliases: TB of the lining of the lung
facts.text: Twenty-five years ago I had tuberculous pleurisy.

findings.name: neck examination
findings.result: Firm, movable, non-tender masses in the right anterior cervical triangle, the largest 3 × 3 × 2 cm; no overlying skin changes.

findings.name: axillary and inguinal lymph node examination
findings.result: Palpable lymph nodes in both axillary and inguinal regions.

findings.name: complete blood count
findings.result: Hemoglobin 7.3 g/dL; WBC 6.2 × 10^9/L with 12.1% eosinophils; platelet count 200 × 10^9/L.

findings.name: fine-needle aspiration cytology of a cervical node
contrast-enhanced CT of the neck and chest
findings.result: Enlarging lymph nodes adjacent to both sternocleidomastoid muscles and numerous nodes (>1 cm) in the axillary, paratracheal, subcarinal, and intrapulmonary regions.

findings.name: CT of the abdomen and pelvis
findings.result: Multiple enhancing lymph nodes in the hepatic hilum, peripancreatic, celiac, and paraaortic regions (largest 4.5 cm).

findings.name: gallium-67 scan
findings.result: Increased uptake in cervical, axillary, paraaortic, iliac, and inguinal lymph nodes.

gold.reasoning: 1. Malignant lymphoma or metastatic cancer were strongly considered because of the widespread lymphadenopathy on imaging — “Clinically, KD may often be confused with malignant lymphoma or other metastatic cancers.” 2. Parasitic infection was evaluated in light of the peripheral eosinophilia — “Stool examinations, including ova and parasite evaluations, were negative.” 3. Tuberculosis was considered given his history and regional lymphadenopathy — “possibly as neoplastic disease or infection, such as tuberculosis, in Asian patients.”
